interface.title: StructDiff Card
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis and reporting: comparing two solved or predicted 3D structures after they have been obtained
interface.what_it_is_for: Superpose a mobile and a reference PDB/mmCIF structure with one US-align global transform, then show which chains correspond, where and how much the structures differ (per-residue displacement, hotspots, 3D patches, gained and lost contacts, rigid-body vs internal motion), and export an auditable result bundle.

data.note: I mostly used the bundled 2HHB → 1HHO example (deoxy vs oxy haemoglobin). It gave TM-score 0.982, RMSD 0.89 Å, 287/287 aligned residues, mappings C→A and D→B, and mobile chains A and B unmatched. I also uploaded the test files 2HHB.pdb (mobile) and 1HHO.pdb (reference) to try a manual chain mapping, then uploaded them the other way round (1HHO mobile, 2HHB reference).

tree.general: Find out where and how two 3D structures of the same molecule differ, and keep a record of the comparison that others can check
tree.specific: Compare a mobile and a reference PDB/mmCIF with US-align and read the StructDiff Card: chain map, residuals, hotspots, contacts, motion decomposition, export bundle

features.name: Two-input comparison setup with optional manual pairing
features.general: Give a 'moving' file and a 'fixed' file, choose whether to use only the first model or all models in each file, optionally state which parts pair with which, and run. An invalid pairing, or a scope the engine cannot handle, is not reported cleanly: a raw error traceback appears low in the side panel while the previous result stays on screen.
features.specific: Upload Structure 1 · mobile and Structure 2 · reference (PDB/CIF/mmCIF), pick Coordinate scope, optionally type a chain mapping such as C:A,D:B, set the US-align timeout, then press Analyze structures, or use the bundled example button. Errors such as 'ValueError: Unknown mobile chain in manual mapping: Z' or 'US-align reported unknown or ambiguous chain: 1,C' show as a Python traceback in the sidebar.
serves_tasks: Upload your own two files, naming one as the item to move and one as the fixed reference
Override the automatic pairing of parts between the two inputs
Choose whether to compare only the first model in each file or all models in it
Set a time limit for the alignment engine
Check how the choice of reference changes the normalised similarity score and the coverage

features.name: Headline similarity, fit-error and coverage strip
features.general: Show the overall similarity score, the fit error, aligned-over-total coverage and the number of matched parts side by side, so a score computed on low coverage cannot be read on its own.
features.specific: Metric strip: TM-score · reference, Global RMSD (Å), Aligned residues (n / total), Mapped chains. Example: 0.982 / 0.89 Å / 287 of 287 / 2; swapped inputs: 0.495 / 0.89 Å / 287 of 574.
steps: read the similarity score normalised by the reference
read the number of matched parts
serves_tasks: Read overall similarity and fit-error scores after one rigid superposition, together with how much of each input was covered
Check how the choice of reference changes the normalised similarity score and the coverage

features.name: Difference-coloured 3D superposition viewer with toggleable layers
features.general: Show two superposed 3D models, coloured by per-element difference on a fixed scale. Layers (reference, unmatched parts, difference vectors, cluster markers) can be hidden or shown alone. Rotate, zoom, hover to read values, reset the camera, save a PNG.
features.specific: Plotly 3D overlay: reference chains in grey, mapped mobile chains coloured 0→≥5 Å, unmatched mobile chains in violet, yellow difference spokes ≥ threshold, P1/P2 patch markers. Legend click hides a trace, double-click isolates it. Hover reads chain:residue and residual, or patch size and peak.
steps: click legend entries to hide/show layers (double-click to isolate: not replayed)
hover a residue or patch marker to read its residual
serves_tasks: Look at both structures superposed in 3D, coloured by how far each residue moved

features.name: Per-position profile with threshold line, smoothed mean and ranked peak regions
features.general: Plot a per-position measurement along an ordered series, with a moving average per group, a threshold line and numbered markers for flagged regions. Pair it with summary statistics and a sortable ranked table of those regions. Box-zoom into a region, hover a marker, autoscale back.
features.specific: Per-residue displacement plot (C→A and D→B residues plus 7-residue means, hotspot threshold 2.00 Å, numbered difference-region diamonds coloured by residual), together with the Difference localization stats (median, 90th percentile, largest, count ≥ threshold) and the ranked region table (chain map, mobile/reference region, mean, peak, high residues). The default y-axis stops at 5 Å, so a region peaking above that (region 1, 5.28 Å) is clipped until you autoscale.
steps: sort the ranked region table by peak
box-zoom the profile on a region
hover a numbered region marker to read the residue pair and value
serves_tasks: Get summary statistics of the differences and a ranked list of the most-changed regions
Plot displacement along the sequence against a threshold to find peaks

features.name: 3D spatial-cluster table of high-difference residues
features.general: Group high-difference elements that sit close together in space, even across groups or far apart in sequence, and list each cluster with its size, groups involved, mean and peak difference, spatial radius and members. Cluster labels match the markers in the 3D view.
features.specific: 3D spatial difference patches table: P1 (4 residues, C/A, mean 3.07, peak 5.28 Å, radius 6.15 Å) and P2 (6 residues, D/B, mean 2.58, peak 4.21 Å, radius 9.26 Å) with member residues; the P1/P2 labels match the patch markers in the 3D overlay
steps: read each patch's size, chains, mean and peak
read its radius and member residues
hover the matching P marker in the 3D view
serves_tasks: Group nearby high-difference residues in space, even across chains or distant sequence

features.name: Gained/lost pairwise contact map with linked table
features.general: Compare the pairwise contacts in two states. Count gained, lost and cross-group changes, plot each change on an index-by-index scatter, and list them in a searchable table whose columns can be hidden or shown.
features.specific: Gained and lost contacts: counts (gained in mobile, lost from mobile, inter-chain gained/lost), a scatter of mapped residue index 1 vs 2 (gained = dots, lost = crosses, larger = inter-chain), and a table (Change, Mobile pair, Reference pair, Mobile Å, Reference Å, Inter-chain) with Search and Show/hide columns
steps: hover a point on the contact map for both distances
show/hide table columns to see the Inter-chain flag (not replayed)
serves_tasks: List the residue contacts that appear or disappear between the two structures

features.name: Rigid-body vs internal deformation decomposition
features.general: For each matched part, refit it locally after the global fit. Split its error into a whole-body component and an internal-shape component, show them as grouped bars, and give a table with centroid shift, rotation correction and a verbal pattern label.
features.specific: Rigid-body motion vs internal deformation: grouped bars per chain mapping (Rigid-body component, Internal deformation in Å) plus a table (Global Å, Rigid-body Å, Internal Å, Centroid shift Å, Correction °, Pattern such as 'well aligned'). The components combine by root-sum-square.
steps: read the grouped bars per chain pair
hover a bar for its value and pattern
scroll the table to centroid shift, correction angle and pattern
serves_tasks: Split each part's movement into whole-body shift versus internal shape change

features.name: Part-correspondence table with unmatched-part warnings and alignment track
features.general: After automatic or manual pairing, list each matched pair with its scores, flag the parts left unpaired and warn when the inputs differ in assembly or part count, and show the aligned sequences as scrollable strips with the unpaired parts marked.
features.specific: Chain mapping table (Mobile, Reference, TM-ref, RMSD Å, Aligned) with the yellow 'Unmatched chains' alert and assembly/chain-count warnings, plus the 'Alignment and unmatched-chain track' sequence strips (hover 'Matched') and 'Mobile A · unmatched' badges
steps: read matched chain pairs and their per-pair scores
read the unmatched-chain and assembly/chain-count warnings
scroll the alignment track along the sequence
hover a residue to see its match status
serves_tasks: Before trusting any score, see which parts of one input pair with which parts of the other, which have no partner, and whether the inputs are flagged as differing in assembly or part count
Check the alignment residue by residue and see which parts were left out

features.name: One-glance summary card
features.general: Gather the input names, headline scores, part pairing, strongest difference region and unpaired parts into a single figure that can be downloaded as vector graphics.
features.specific: Publication card (2HHB.pdb → 1HHO.pdb, TM-score, RMSD, chain mapping, strongest region, unmatched chains) with a 'Publication card SVG' download
serves_tasks: Get a one-glance summary figure for a paper or slide

features.name: Per-file result download panel
features.general: Offer each result table, summary, figure, structure file and viewer script as its own download, so only what is needed is taken into other tools.
features.specific: Download result bundle: residue/chain/hotspot/contact/motion/patch CSVs, contact and difference summary JSON, displacement plot SVG, reference/aligned/difference-colored PDB, PyMOL view_difference.pml, complete result.json
steps: pick the table, structure or script needed
open the file in another tool (e.g. load the .pml in PyMOL)
serves_tasks: Export the tables, structures and a viewer script for further analysis

features.name: Provenance and raw engine log panel
features.general: Show the engine version, the exact command run and a hash of each input file, plus the engine's raw output, so others can reproduce the run or confirm which files were used.
features.specific: 'Reproducibility and raw US-align output' expander: engine (US-align 20260527), command (USalign … -mm 1 -ter 1 -full T -m matrix.txt), mobile and reference SHA-256 hashes, raw per-chain log
steps: read the engine version and command
compare the input SHA-256 hashes with your files
serves_tasks: Check exactly how the result was computed and confirm which input files were used

screens_never_reached: A successful biological-assembly comparison of uploaded files. With 'All models / biological assembly', Analyze on 2HHB/1HHO failed with 'ValueError: US-align reported unknown or ambiguous chain: 1,C' (screens/039.webp, screens/040.webp), and the earlier result stayed on screen.

Any example result reflecting the manual mapping or the biological-assembly scope. Pressing 'Load 2HHB → 1HHO example' with mapping A:A,B:B (screens/035.webp) or with biological assembly selected (screens/042.webp) gave the same C→A/D→B result. The example appears to ignore these sidebar settings, though I could not confirm this from the interface.
Inter-chain contact changes: both runs reported 0 inter-chain gained or lost, so the larger inter-chain symbols were never shown.
Gap rows in the alignment track (residues present in only one file): the example aligned 287/287 with no gaps, so how gaps are drawn was never seen.
not_done: Did not download every bundle file. I skipped Chain mapping CSV, Difference hotspots CSV, Contact changes CSV, Contact summary JSON, Spatial patches CSV, Difference summary JSON, Displacement plot SVG, and the Reference, Aligned mobile and Difference-colored PDBs to stay within the action budget. The ones I did download (residue_mapping.csv, motion_decomposition.csv, publication_card.svg, view_difference.pml, result.json, plot-image.png) all saved, and I read result.json, view_difference.pml and residue_mapping.csv.
Did not upload mmCIF files: only PDB test files were available.
Did not run with timeout 0 (unlimited) or test a timeout that actually expires. I only raised the value from 1800 to 2100 and did not run an analysis afterwards.
Did not try the fullscreen buttons on tables and plots, or the Orbital/Turntable rotation and Pan mode buttons on the 3D toolbar.

Analyze on the uploads with 'All models / biological assembly' crashed with a raw traceback ('ValueError: US-align reported unknown or ambiguous chain: 1,C') in the sidebar, and the old result stayed shown (screens/039.webp, screens/040.webp). This is a noted defect, not a working path.
Loading the example with 'All models / biological assembly' selected gave the same result as the first-model scope (screens/042.webp), so the setting had no visible effect there.

open_fixes: A successful 'All models / biological assembly' comparison needs a new run with inputs whose model or chain naming US-align accepts. The only try crashed, so the scope's real effect on the results is still unknown.
mmCIF input needs a new run with mmCIF files. Only PDB files were available.
Gap rows in the alignment track need a pair with unequal coverage (e.g. a truncated or partially missing chain), because the example aligned 287/287 with no gaps.
Timeout behaviour (0 = unlimited, or a timeout that actually expires) and whether the timeout is recorded in result.json need a new run.
The f2 isolate/zoom/reset/PNG steps and the f4 show/hide-columns step should be replayed by a second agent to confirm them; the contact-changes CSV download was never tried.
Inter-chain contact symbols need an input pair with inter-chain contact changes, because both runs reported 0.
